artboards.title: C — One canvas, all the way down
F — The building is the map
H — The estate as it changes

annotations.text:
Eight answers to ONE question: how do you navigate a system with this many dimensions (physical / L2 / L3 / power, campus → building → closet → rack → device → port, ownership, IP, link type)?

A–D are the textbook shapes. E–H are the ones I would actually argue for.

Deliberately rough. Judge the navigation idea, not the pixels.

True in ALL EIGHT, so not a differentiator:

• Racks group, one by default, size is editable
• Equipment carries its real port complement from the engine — count, position, and type (copper / fibre / power)
• Drag a port to a port to cable it
• A cable can end in a PORTAL — up or down — meaning it leaves this view. Not an unknown, just elsewhere
• Owner is a property of equipment, filterable everywhere
• Physical / L2 / L3 are the same graph, drawn differently — never separate drawings that drift apart

Second batch — my own.

E, G and H are not really shells; they are MODES that would live inside whichever shell wins, and I have said so on each. F is the only one of the four that could be the whole shell.

MY RECOMMENDATION, if you want one:

SHELL = F (the building is the map) with A's layer bar across the top and B's estate tree in the left rail. Everything you described is a PLACE — closets, NOCs, sublet floors, risers — and F puts place first. It is also the most Lucidchart-like of the eight: you draw rooms, drop racks, run cables. That is your priority 1.

MODES inside it:
• E (follow the wire) — the trace and the teaching view. Opens when you click a flagged policy in the config checker.
• H (time) — a scrubber you can pull down over anything.
• G (two truths) — an optional split of any canvas.

D is a search box inside this, not a shell. C is the beautiful risk — I would not bet the product on it.

Honest cost: a pure L3 question across sites with no building needs a blank canvas too. That is just A on an empty sheet, so the shell must allow a canvas with no floor plan behind it.
